# OpenCode Token Usage **See what every turn actually costs — right under the reply.** A zero-config GUI plugin for **OpenCode Desktop V2** (2.2.3+): per-turn tokens, cache hit rate and RMB cost. Requires the V2 desktop app; it does not work in the TUI. [![CI](https://github.com/AquariusCZ/opencode-token-usage-gui/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/AquariusCZ/opencode-token-usage-gui/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/AquariusCZ/opencode-token-usage-gui?label=release&color=111827)](https://github.com/AquariusCZ/opencode-token-usage-gui/releases/latest) [![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-MIT-blue.svg)](LICENSE) [![OpenCode Desktop](https://img.shields.io/badge/OpenCode%20Desktop-2.2.3%2B-111827)](https://opencode.ai/) [![PRs welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen.svg)](https://github.com/AquariusCZ/opencode-token-usage-gui/issues) [Install](#install) · [Features](#features) · [Configuration](#configuration) · [How it works](#how-it-works) · [FAQ](#faq) · [中文](README.zh-CN.md)
```sh opencode plugin add github:AquariusCZ/opencode-token-usage-gui ``` Then reload the window (`Ctrl/Cmd + R`) or run `opencode service restart`. Full options are under [Install](#install). ![OpenCode Desktop with a per-turn token footer](assets/screenshot-en.png) *Illustrative English mock of the footer and details card. Not a real session screenshot. The illustration shows `popoverSide: "right"`; the default is left.* > OpenCode Desktop shows the latest request and the session total. It does not show what **this turn** cost. > This plugin adds the missing line. ## The 10-second version ```text This turn · Input 15,733 · Output 6,250 · Cache read 10,300,544 · Cache hit 99.8% · Total 10,332,638 · ¥0.288 ``` Hover the line — or focus its info button — for a readable breakdown: ```text Turn breakdown · 10,332,638 tokens · ¥0.288 (≈ $0.0431) [■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■■] 99.7% cache read Input 15,733 Output 6,250 Reasoning 10,111 Cache read 10,300,544 Cache write 0 Cache hit 99.8% 21 model requests · 2m 15s · Exchange rate 6.68 · manual ``` Click the info button to pin the card while you read or copy it. The preview stays open when you move onto it — an invisible 8 px bridge covers the gap — so there is nothing to chase; the pinned card closes with Escape or a click outside. Escape closes it from any non-editing surface; text fields, editors, selects, menus/listboxes and dialogs keep Escape for the app. ## Why not just use the built-in context panel? The built-in panel answers **“how big is the context right now?”** This plugin answers **“what did this turn cost, and why?”** | | Built-in context panel | This plugin | CLI `debug.turn_tokens` | | --- | :---: | :---: | :---: | | Latest request | ✅ | ❌ (per-turn) | — | | Per-turn total | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | Cache hit rate | ❌ | ✅ | — | | Per-turn cost | ❌ | ✅ CNY / USD | ❌ | | Inline under every reply | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | | Works in the desktop GUI | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | A turn is not one request. In a long agent loop it can contain 20+ assistant requests and tool calls. Showing only the last assistant message hides most of the cost. This plugin sums the whole turn, then shows the numbers that actually change the bill. ## Features - **Per-turn, not per-message.** One footer per turn, aggregating every assistant request and tool loop. - **A details card that is actually readable.** Hover or focus the footer for a theme-aware card with a token composition bar, a six-cell metric grid, request count, wall time, and the exchange-rate source. The card stays open while your pointer is over it (an invisible bridge covers the gap) and can be pinned with the info button for persistent reading and copying. It opens on the configured side of the footer (left by default), then below it, then above, so it does not cover the turn's step rows on a wide window; it clamps to the viewport and repositions on scroll and resize. - **One capsule per turn, live in place.** Each turn's capsule is rendered under that turn's reply and updates while the turn is thinking or running tools; completed turns keep their capsule. The capsule appears with the first usage sample — a queued or steered prompt never creates a zero-value "This turn" line. - **One session capsule, always in the dock.** The composer dock above the input always shows one session-wide capsule labeled "Session" once the session has usage — while a turn runs, while it is idle, and while messages are queued. Token and cost totals come from the app's session ledger — `session.get().tokens` plus `session.cost()`, including title/compaction and, when the API is available, subagent usage — so they are lifetime billed totals, not the sum of the loaded transcript. The inline capsule shows tokens, cost and cache hit; hover it for the full session card, which adds requests and active time. Turn, request and active-time counts cover the loaded transcript and are marked "loaded" when older message pages exist. The dock never switches to a per-turn capsule: the two capsule types are separate. - **Above the app's normal layers.** The details card is rendered in a fixed body portal at z-index 2147483000, above the timeline, later messages and the composer, so normal stacking contexts cannot cover or clip it. An app-level modal/dialog may still sit above it. - **A footer you can hit.** The visible line is a padded pill with a dedicated info button whose hit area extends past the glyph; no need to land on a single 12 px line. - **Keyboard accessible.** Tab to the info button, press Enter or Space to pin, Escape or an outside click to close. Escape closes the card from any non-editing surface; text fields, contenteditable editors, selects, menus/listboxes and dialogs keep Escape for the app. `prefers-reduced-motion` disables the card transition. - **Live count-up.** Continuous mode samples the store at 100 ms while running and follows the target with a 60 Hz first-order lag; a new sample changes the target without restarting the animation, so the counter reads as one continuous motion. An `interval` mode keeps the old discrete refresh + tween behavior. Respects `prefers-reduced-motion`. - **Cache-aware.** Shows cache reads and the cache hit rate — the metric that explains most of the cost difference on DeepSeek and Anthropic models. - **RMB by default.** Converts the app's USD cost with a manual or daily-cached rate; the original USD amount stays in the card. `"currency": "USD"` switches back, `"auto"` follows the UI language. - **Revert-aware.** Messages hidden by an undo/revert boundary are excluded from totals. - **Stale-proof.** Stale footers are pruned on every sync, so a session switch, a revert, or a row the app removed cannot leave a ghost line behind. - **Bilingual.** Follows the app locale: 中文 or English. - **Compact or detailed.** Default shows the decision-making numbers; `detailed` adds reasoning tokens and cache writes to the visible line. The card always shows the full breakdown. - **Zero runtime dependencies.** One built CJS file. No telemetry, no API keys, and no network requests unless you explicitly opt into `usdToCny: "auto"`. - **Safe failure.** If the app's internal DOM changes, the plugin logs one warning and stays quiet instead of breaking the timeline. - **Fast.** Aggregating 2,000 messages takes about 3 ms in the test suite; the sampler runs at 100 ms while a session is running (1000 ms idle), and the card only writes DOM when its data changes. ## Install ### The 30-second version (GitHub) ```sh opencode plugin add github:AquariusCZ/opencode-token-usage-gui ``` Then reload the desktop window (`Ctrl/Cmd + R`) or restart the service: ```sh opencode service restart ``` ### Manual install ```sh git clone https://github.com/AquariusCZ/opencode-token-usage-gui.git \ ~/.config/opencode/plugins/opencode-token-usage-gui ``` Windows PowerShell: ```powershell git clone https://github.com/AquariusCZ/opencode-token-usage-gui.git ` "$env:USERPROFILE\.config\opencode\plugins\opencode-token-usage-gui" ``` OpenCode discovers immediate plugin directories under `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`. If the footer does not appear, open **Settings → Extensions → Plugins** and use **Reload**, or run `opencode service restart`. ### Verify 1. A capsule appears under each turn and updates in place while the turn streams. The composer dock always shows one Session summary. 2. **Settings → Extensions → Plugins** lists `token-usage-gui` and its switch is on. 3. `opencode plugin list` shows `token-usage-gui`. 4. If something is off, check `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` for `token-usage-gui`. ### Uninstall Remove the directory and reload. To disable only the desktop UI, use the plugin's switch in **Settings → Extensions → Plugins**. To remove a package install: ```sh opencode plugin remove opencode-token-usage-gui ``` ## Configuration Options go in the plugin entry of `opencode.json(c)`: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "opencode-token-usage-gui", "options": { "compact": false, "detailed": false, "showCost": true, "popoverSide": "left", "animate": true, "refreshMode": "continuous", // default; "interval" switches to refreshMs/tweenMs "sampleMs": 100, "smoothMs": 250, "refreshMs": 500, // interval mode only "tweenMs": 550, // interval mode only "currency": "CNY", "usdToCny": 6.68 } } ] } ``` | Option | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `compact` | `false` | Show only input, output, total and cost. | | `detailed` | `false` | Also show reasoning tokens and cache writes on the visible line. | | `showCost` | `true` | Show the per-turn cost. | | `popoverSide` | `"left"` | Side for the details card: `"left"` or `"right"`. The chosen side is tried first; if it does not fit, the card falls back below, then above. It never switches to the other side. | | `animate` | `true` | Animate the numbers. Set `false` to snap in both modes. | | `refreshMode` | `"continuous"` | `"continuous"` (fluid counter) or `"interval"` (discrete refresh + tween). | | `sampleMs` | `100` | Continuous mode: data sample interval while the session is running, clamped to 50–1000 ms. Idle sessions sample at 1000 ms. | | `smoothMs` | `250` | Continuous mode: first-order lag time constant, clamped to 50–2000 ms. Larger = softer/slower. | | `refreshMs` | `500` | Interval mode: refresh interval, clamped to 16–5000 ms. `16.67` = 60 Hz; intended for experiments. | | `tweenMs` | `550` | Interval mode: tween duration, clamped to 0–2000 ms. | | `currency` | `"CNY"` | `"CNY"`, `"USD"`, or `"auto"`. `auto` uses CNY for a Chinese UI and USD otherwise. | | `usdToCny` | `6.68` | A number (manual rate, no network) or `"auto"` (daily cached rate; see below). | A local directory works the same way: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "./plugins/opencode-token-usage-gui", "options": { "compact": true } } ] } ``` ### Card side The details card opens to the left of the footer by default. Set `"popoverSide": "right"` to prefer the right gutter. The chosen side is tried first. On a narrow window where it does not fit, the card falls back below the footer, then above it; it does not switch to the opposite side. This keeps the configured direction predictable. ### Currency and exchange rate `message.cost` is always USD from the provider. The footer is a **display conversion**, not a second billing source. - `currency: "CNY"` (default) shows `¥`. - `currency: "USD"` shows the native `$` amount. - `currency: "auto"` uses CNY in a Chinese UI and USD otherwise. - `usdToCny: 6.68` is a manual rate. It is deterministic and makes **no network request**. - `usdToCny: "auto"` fetches the daily USD→CNY rate from `open.er-api.com`, caches it for 24 hours, and falls back to the last cached rate or the manual `6.68` when offline. Only this opt-in mode uses the network. The details card always tells you which rate was used: ```text Exchange rate 6.68 · manual Exchange rate 6.72 · auto (2026-10-30) Exchange rate 6.68 · fallback ``` Set `usdToCny` to your actual billing rate if you want the number to match your invoice exactly. ### Refresh modes `refreshMode` is the switch: - **`"continuous"` (default)** — the sampler reads the store every `sampleMs` (100 ms) while the session is running, and every 1000 ms when idle. The display runs at 60 Hz and follows the latest target with a first-order lag (`smoothMs`, 250 ms). A new sample only changes the target; it never restarts the animation, so the counter reads as one continuous motion from the first token to the final total. - **`"interval"`** — the old behavior: read every `refreshMs` (500 ms), then tween to the new value over `tweenMs` (550 ms). Use this if you prefer visible step changes or a fixed sampling cadence. `animate: false` disables both filters and snaps to the target. Why this split: the display can update at 60 Hz, but the data can only change when the session store changes. Polling the store at 60 Hz is wasteful (see the measurement below); sampling at 100 ms and filtering at 60 Hz gives the same visual continuity at a fraction of the CPU. Measured on a ~200-message session (Windows 11, OpenCode Desktop 2.2.3): `interval` at 500 ms used about **1.6% of one CPU core**; polling at 16.67 ms (60 Hz) used about **12.7%** over the same 20-second window; `continuous` with 100 ms sampling used about **2.7%**. The count-up animation was already 60 Hz via `requestAnimationFrame`, so 60 Hz *data* polling bought no extra smoothness. Continuous mode keeps the 60 Hz animation but samples at 100 ms, so it gets the smooth motion without the 60 Hz polling cost. The timer pauses while the window is hidden and refreshes immediately when it becomes visible again. A debounced `MutationObserver` still reattaches the footer when the app re-renders the timeline. ### Display modes | Mode | Visible line | | --- | --- | | Default | input · output · cache read · cache hit · total · cost | | `compact: true` | input · output · total · cost | | `detailed: true` | input · output · reasoning · cache read · cache write · cache hit · total · cost | The details card always shows the full breakdown, including the composition bar, request count and wall time. ## What the numbers mean The total follows OpenCode's own definition: ```text input + output + reasoning + cache.read + cache.write ``` - **Turn** is delimited by the app's idle markers: it opens at the first user prompt of an execution and closes at the next idle marker. Prompts steered in or queued during the turn belong to it; synthetic/system/compaction notices never split a running turn. An orphan notice (for example a subagent result with no user prompt) owns the assistant usage that follows. Transcripts recorded before idle markers existed fall back to user-message boundaries. - **Cache hit rate** is `cache.read / (input + cache.read + cache.write)`. It describes how much of the prompt was served from cache. - **Cost** comes from the app's per-request `message.cost` (USD). CNY is a display conversion; it is not a second billing source. - **Requests** counts assistant messages with a usage record, not individual tool calls. - **Duration** runs from the first assistant request to the last completed one in the turn. If a turn has no reported cost (free models, some providers), the cost is hidden and the token counts still show. ## How it works ```text user message │ ├─ assistant request 1 ─┐ ├─ tool call │ ├─ assistant request 2 ├─ one turn ├─ tool call │ └─ assistant request 3 ─┘ │ ▼ input + output + reasoning + cache.read + cache.write ``` 1. The plugin reads the active session's message list from the app's client store. 2. It groups assistant messages into turns — idle-delimited in current sessions, user-delimited in older transcripts — and sums `tokens` and `cost`. 3. It finds the rendered assistant content container (`[data-slot="session-turn-assistant-content"]`) and appends a footer node. 4. A 100 ms sampler (1000 ms when idle) keeps values fresh; a `MutationObserver` re-attaches the footer when the app re-renders the timeline; `requestAnimationFrame` animates changes. 5. Each turn's footer is appended to its assistant content and updates in place while the app reports `session.status` as `running`; it never moves into the composer dock. Hovering opens the fixed body-portal card at z-index 2147483000, preferring the configured side (left by default), then below, then above. The follow timer skips a hidden window. 6. The composer dock always shows a synthetic "Session" footer — one per session — once the session has usage. Token and cost totals come from the app's session ledger: `session.get(id).tokens` and `session.cost(id)` (family-aware for a root, own usage for a child), folded over the session and, when the API exists, its family. The ledger includes title/compaction usage, reverted usage (a revert does not refund) and subagent usage, so the summary is a lifetime billed total and can exceed the sum of the per-turn footers. Turn count, requests and active time still come from `summarizeTurns(turns)` over the loaded transcript, and are labeled "loaded" when `message.more(id)` reports older pages. `message.sync`/`loadMore` are never called, so reading the summary never mutates the transcript or the scroll position. There is no zero-value placeholder before the first usage, and the summary is never replaced by a per-turn capsule. There is no official message-footer slot in the GUI plugin API, so the last step is DOM injection. That is the intentionally fragile part: if a future OpenCode release renames the slot, the footer disappears (the plugin logs one warning) rather than corrupting the timeline. The selector, footer, placement and aggregation logic are isolated in `src/gui.cjs`, `src/footer.cjs`, `src/placement.cjs` and `src/core.cjs`, so adapting is usually a one-line change. ## Compatibility - Tested with **OpenCode Desktop 2.2.3** on Windows 11. - Requires the V2 desktop app; it does not work in the TUI. - The GUI plugin API is marked experimental by OpenCode and may change between releases. - The DOM-based rendering should work on macOS and Linux, but those platforms have not been tested. For the TUI, use the CLI's built-in `debug.turn_tokens` or one of the terminal-only token plugins. ## Privacy - No network requests by default, no telemetry, no API keys. - Reads only the local session state that the desktop app already has in memory. - The default exchange rate is a manual constant; it is not fetched at runtime. - `usdToCny: "auto"` is the only network path: one request per day to `open.er-api.com`, cached for 24 hours. Leave it on the default manual value for a fully offline plugin. ## FAQ **Does it send my prompts or session data anywhere?** No session data is sent anywhere. The only network request is the opt-in daily USD→CNY rate fetch (`usdToCny: "auto"`); the default plugin is fully offline. **Why per-turn instead of per-message?** A turn can contain many assistant requests and tool loops. Per-message numbers look smaller but are misleading. Use `detailed` if you want more metrics on the visible line. **Where is the total for the whole session?** The composer dock always shows it. The "Session" capsule is the session ledger total; per-turn capsules in the conversation show attribution. **Can I see reasoning tokens?** Yes: set `detailed: true`, or open the details card. Reasoning is always in the card. **Can I use USD instead of RMB?** Yes: set `"currency": "USD"`. The card still shows the original USD amount when CNY is selected. **How do I keep the card open?** Click the small info button at the end of the footer. The pinned card is selectable, so you can copy numbers; click the button again, press Escape, or click outside to close it. Escape closes it from any non-editing surface; text fields, editors, selects, menus/listboxes and dialogs keep Escape for the app. **Can I choose which side the card opens on?** Yes: set `"popoverSide": "left"` (default) or `"popoverSide": "right"`. The chosen side is tried first, then below, then above; it does not switch to the other side. **Why is the card never cut off by later messages?** It is rendered into a fixed portal on `document.body` at a very high z-index (2147483000), above the app's normal stacking contexts, not inside the scrolling timeline row. Later messages, row clipping and the composer cannot paint over it. **Why is the cost zero?** The provider did not report a cost for that request. Free models and some local providers do not report one. **Will it survive an OpenCode update?** Usually yes; the selector is the fragile part. If the footer disappears after an update, open an issue with your OpenCode version and a screenshot. **How is the exchange rate determined?** By default it is the manual `usdToCny` number (`6.68`). With `"usdToCny": "auto"` it fetches the daily rate, caches it for 24 hours, and falls back to the last cache or `6.68`. The details card shows the rate, its source, and the date when it was automatic. **Can I change how often the footer refreshes?** Yes: `sampleMs` (50–1000, default 100) controls continuous sampling and `smoothMs` (50–2000, default 250) controls the follow speed; interval mode uses `refreshMs` (16–5000, default 500) and `tweenMs` (0–2000, default 550). The timer pauses while the window is hidden. **Does it work in the TUI?** No. The TUI has `debug.turn_tokens`; this plugin is for the desktop GUI. ## Roadmap - Per-message mode for people who want a footer under every assistant message. - Context usage percentage in the details card. - CSV/JSON export of turn usage. - Provider-specific price tables instead of a single USD→CNY rate. - A small settings panel instead of JSON options. - A selector health check that reports when the app's DOM changes. Ideas and PRs are welcome. If the plugin saves you a scroll, a star helps other people find it. ## Development ```sh npm install npm test # pure-logic tests, Node's built-in runner npm run build # bundles src/gui.cjs -> dist/gui-experimental.cjs npm run check # build + test ``` Layout: ```text src/core.cjs pure aggregation and formatting src/footer.cjs footer DOM, details card and interactions src/placement.cjs DOM-free card placement math src/gui.cjs plugin lifecycle, DOM discovery, animation dist/gui-experimental.cjs built single-file CJS entry (committed) test/core.test.cjs aggregation and formatter tests test/placement.test.cjs card placement edge cases scripts/build.mjs esbuild bundle assets/mock.html interactive illustrative mock ``` For local development, copy `dist/gui-experimental.cjs` into your plugin directory after each build, or point the plugin at the repo directory and reload. The app watches the built file and reloads the GUI for local plugin directories. ## Community Questions / launch feedback: [OpenCode Discord](https://opencode.ai/discord) · [Issues](https://github.com/AquariusCZ/opencode-token-usage-gui/issues) ## Contributing - Open an issue for bugs, selector breakage, or feature requests. - Keep `dist/gui-experimental.cjs` in sync with `src/`; CI checks it. - Run `npm test` before opening a PR. - If an OpenCode update breaks the footer, include the app version and a screenshot. ## License MIT © [AquariusCZ](https://github.com/AquariusCZ) --- [中文说明](README.zh-CN.md)

15,733 输出 6,250 推理 10,111 缓存读 10,300,544 缓存写 0 缓存命中 99.8% 21 次模型请求 · 2m 15s · 汇率 6.68 · 手动 ``` 点击 ⓘ 按钮可以把卡片钉住，方便阅读或复制；未钉住时卡片也能直接悬停——卡片和 footer 之间有一条 不可见的 8px 悬停桥，鼠标移上去不会消失；移开自动收起，钉住后按 Esc 或点击卡片外关闭（焦点不在输入框、编辑器、 下拉框、菜单/列表或对话框里时按 Esc 关闭；这些地方 Esc 留给应用）。 ## 为什么不直接用右上角的上下文面板？ 上下文面板回答的是**「现在上下文有多大」**；这个插件回答的是**「这一轮花了多少、钱花在哪」**。 | | 内置上下文面板 | 这个插件 | CLI `debug.turn_tokens` | | --- | :---: | idle 标记分界：一次执行的第一条用户 prompt 开始，到下一个 idle 标记结束。这一轮中途引导或排队的 prompt 属于本轮；synthetic/system/compaction 只作为通知，不会切断正在运行的轮次；没有 user prompt 的孤儿通知（例如子代理结果）会承接其后的 assistant 用量。早于 idle 标记的旧会话回退到用户消息边界。 - **缓存命中率**：`cache.read / (input + cache.read + cache.write)`，表示 prompt 里有多大比例来自缓存。 - **费用**：来自应用上报的每请求 `message.cost`（美元）。人民币只是显示换算，不是第二套计费。 - **请求次数**：有 usage 记录的 assistant 消息数，不是工具调用次数。 - **耗时**：这一轮第一条 assistant 请求到最后一条完成的时间。 如果模型/供应商没有上报费用（免费模型、部分本地 provider），费用会隐藏，token 仍然显示。 ## 实现方式 ```text user message │ ├─ assistant request 1 ─┐ ├─ tool call │ ├─ assistant request 2 ├─ 一轮 ├─ tool call │ └─ assistant request 3 ─┘ │ ▼ input + output + reasoning + cache.read + cache.write ``` 1. 从应用的客户端 store 读取当前会话的消息列表； 2. 按轮分组 assistant 消息——当前会话按 idle 分界，旧对话按用户消息分界——并累加 `tokens` 和 `cost`； 3. 找到渲染出来的 assistant 内容容器（`[data-slot="session-turn-assistant-content"]`），把 footer 节点挂进去； 4. 100ms 采样（空闲 1000ms）保持数据新鲜；`MutationObserver` 在应用重渲染时把 footer 挂回去；`requestAnimationFrame` 做数字动画； 5. 每轮的 footer - **First-step summary.** The summary keeps the transcript totals until the session ledger reports tokens, so it no
  longer disappears on the first step.

# Launch playbook

A working plan for getting `opencode-token-usage-gui` in front of the people who would actually use it.
Everything below assumes one rule: the repository is the product page, and every channel points back to it.

## 1. First principles

Promotion is **relevance × trust × low-friction install**. If any factor is zero, the post does nothing.

- **Relevance.** The plugin solves a narrow, concrete problem: OpenCode Desktop shows the latest request and the
  session total, but not what *this turn* cost. Every channel should lead with that gap, not with "a new plugin".
- **Trust.** A public repo with a readable README, a real screenshot, passing CI, an MIT license and an author who
  answers questions. No inflated numbers, no fake testimonials.
- **Low friction.** One command, then reload. If a reader needs more than 30 seconds to see a capsule, the post
  failed. Do not send people to npm; the package name is a placeholder.

Operating rules that follow from this:

- **One canonical release page.** The GitHub release is the source of truth. Channel posts are short pointers to it.
- **No spray-and-pray.** Five relevant channels done well beat twenty copy-pastes. One post per channel.
- **Let people try in 30 seconds.** Install command first, caveats second, architecture last.
- **Answer issues fast.** The first week's issue response time is the real launch metric.

## 2. Positioning

### One-liner

> Per-turn token, cache and cost capsules for every OpenCode Desktop V2 reply, plus an always-on session total in the composer dock.

### 30-second pitch

OpenCode Desktop tells you how big the context is and what the session has cost so far. It does not tell you what
the reply you are looking at actually cost. This plugin adds one compact line under each turn: input, output, cache
reads, cache hit rate, total tokens and RMB cost. Each turn's capsule stays under its reply and updates live while
the model is thinking or running tools; the composer dock always shows the session summary. A queued or steered
prompt never creates a zero capsule. Hover for a theme-native card with a composition bar, six metrics, request
count and active time. One `opencode plugin add` command, zero runtime dependencies, no network by default.

### Three audience angles

**1. OpenCode Desktop users paying for DeepSeek or Anthropic models.**
The bill is dominated by cache reads and cache hit rate, and those are invisible in the normal UI. Lead with the
cache-aware line and the per-turn cost. This is the largest and most motivated audience.

**2. V2 GUI plugin developers.**
There is no official message-footer slot in the experimental GUI plugin API, so this is a real, working example of
DOM injection into the desktop app: slot discovery, `MutationObserver` re-attachment, fixed body-portal overlays,
theme tokens, and graceful failure when a selector moves. Lead with "a working reference, not a hello world".

**3. Cost- and observability-minded users.**
They already watch context size; they want per-turn attribution plus a lifetime session ledger. Lead with the
distinction between "sum of the transcript" and "what the session was billed", including compaction and subagents.

## 9. FAQ and objections

**Is it safe? Does it send my data anywhere?**
No network by default, no telemetry, no API keys. It reads the session state the desktop app already holds in
memory. The only network path is opting into `usdToCny: "auto"`, which fetches a daily USD→CNY rate from
`open.er-api.com` and caches it for 24 hours.

**Isn't DOM injection fragile?**
Yes, intentionally so. The GUI plugin API has no message-footer slot, so the last step is DOM injection. If a
future desktop release renames the slot, the footer disappears and the plugin logs one warning; it does not corrupt
the timeline. Selector, footer, placement and aggregation live in separate files, so adapting is usually a one-line
change. A selector health check is on the roadmap.

**Does it work in the TUI?**
No. It is a desktop GUI plugin for the V2 app. For the TUI, use the CLI's built-in `debug.turn_tokens`.

**Which models/providers does it support?**
All of them, because it reads the app's own per-request usage and cost. Cache metrics are most useful on providers
that report cache reads (DeepSeek, Anthropic). If a provider reports no cost, the cost is hidden and tokens still
show.

**Why is the session summary larger than the sum of the per-turn capsules?**
The summary comes from the app's session ledger, so it includes title/compaction usage, reverted usage (a revert
does not refund) and, where the API is available, subagent usage. The ledger is a lifetime billed total, not the sum
of the loaded transcript. Turn/request/active-time counts come from the loaded transcript and are marked "loaded"
when older pages exist.

**Is the RMB number a second bill?**
No. Cost comes from the app as USD; CNY is a display conversion at a manual or daily-cached rate. The USD amount
stays in the details card.

**Why not install from npm?**
The npm name is a `0.0.0-stage` placeholder. GitHub is the supported install path:
`opencode plugin add github:AquariusCZ/opencode-token-usage-gui`.

**Is this an official OpenCode plugin?**
No. It is a community plugin, MIT-licensed, built against the experimental V2 GUI plugin API.

# v0.3.0 — per-turn token, cache and cost capsules for OpenCode Desktop V2

> Superseded by [v0.3.1](release-0.3.1.md): the dock now always shows the session summary, and per-turn capsules stay in the transcript.

OpenCode Desktop shows the latest request and the session total. It does not show what **this turn** cost.
This release adds the missing line — and a readable card behind it.

## What it does

- **One capsule per turn.** Input, output, cache reads, cache hit rate, total tokens and RMB cost, under the reply
  they belong to. The whole agent loop is included, not just the last assistant message.
- **A live capsule while work is in flight.** While the model is thinking or running tools, the capsule sits in the
  composer dock, starts at zero and follows the turn. When the turn settles, it moves under the reply.
- **A session summary when the work is done.** Idle session, no pending or queued message: the dock shows a
  session-wide capsule with ledger totals, requests and active time. Starting the next turn replaces it with the
  live capsule.
- **A details card worth hovering.** Theme-native card with a composition bar, six metrics, request count, wall
  time and the exchange-rate source. Pin it with the info button; Escape or an outside click closes it.
- **`popoverSide`.** Prefer the left gutter (default) or the right; the card falls below or above when the chosen
  side does not fit, and never jumps to the opposite side.
- **Theme-native and keyboard accessible.** Colors come from the desktop's own v2 tokens in light and dark mode.
  Tab / Enter / Space pin, Escape closes from non-editing surfaces, `prefers-reduced-motion` is honored.
- **Zero runtime dependencies.** One built CJS file, no telemetry, no API keys, no network requests unless you opt
  into `usdToCny: "auto"` for a daily FX rate.

```sh
opencode plugin add github:AquariusCZ/opencode-token-usage-gui
```

Reload the desktop window with `Ctrl/Cmd + R`, or restart the service:

# v0.3.1 — one session summary in the dock, per-turn capsules in the transcript

This release fixes a v0.3.0 edge case: a queued or steered prompt could create a zero-value "This turn" capsule in
the composer dock, and the dock could flip between a per-turn line and the session summary. The dock now always
shows the session summary; per-turn capsules stay under their turn.

## What changed

- **Two capsule types, cleanly separated.** One **Session** capsule in the composer dock above the input, and one
  capsule under each turn in the transcript.
- **The dock is always the session summary.** Once the session has usage, the "Session" capsule is visible while a
  turn runs, while the session is idle, and while messages are queued. It is never replaced by a per-turn capsule.
- **Per-turn capsules update in place.** The active turn's capsule updates under its reply while the turn is
  thinking or running tools; a queued or steered prompt never creates a zero-value capsule.
- **Turns follow the app's idle markers.** A turn opens at the first user prompt of an execution and closes at the
  next `idle` marker. Steers and delivered queued prompts belong to the running turn; synthetic, system and
  compaction notices never split a running turn; an orphan notice owns the assistant usage that follows.
  Transcripts without idle markers (older sessions) fall back to user-message boundaries, so their history is
  preserved.
- **Steer rows track the turn.** Rows whose `data-message-id` is the delivered steer id now resolve to the turn, so
  the capsule follows the live end of the turn.
- **First-step summary.** The summary keeps the transcript totals until the session ledger reports tokens, so it no
  longer disappears on the first step.
- **Grammar.** The card says "1 turn" instead of "1 turns".
- **45 tests.**
